title: A Special Shabbat with Guests from Israel
body:
Shabbat is always a special time at the Nasenyi Jewish Community. It is a time for prayer, Torah, learning, fellowship, and rest.

On Saturday, 8 August 2026, our Shabbat became even more meaningful as we welcomed David Yair and Itai Mayar, guests from Israel who were visiting our community.

Their presence gave the congregation an opportunity to experience Shabbat together with fellow Jews from Israel and to strengthen the friendship between our communities.

Torah at the Heart of Shabbat

One of the most memorable moments came during the Torah service.

David was invited to read from the Torah. He read fluently in Hebrew, giving the congregation the opportunity to hear the Torah chanted in its original language.

It was a beautiful moment for the community.

At Nasenyi, Torah reading is not only about hearing Hebrew. It is also about ensuring that the congregation understands and participates in the learning.

Our community normally reads the first Aliyah in Hebrew and continues the remaining Aliyot in Luganda. This approach helps make the Torah accessible to everyone in the congregation.

For us, Torah should not simply be heard. It should also be understood.

Learning From One Another

David and Itai also shared Divrei Torah with the congregation.

Their teachings added another important dimension to the Shabbat. We were able to listen, learn, ask questions, reflect, and share perspectives.

Such encounters are valuable because Jewish communities around the world have different experiences and traditions, yet remain connected through Torah and Jewish life.

The Abayudaya communities in Uganda have developed strong connections with Jewish communities outside Uganda, including communities in Israel and elsewhere. These relationships continue to create opportunities for learning and strengthening Jewish identity.

A Shabbat of Friendship

Beyond the prayers and Torah service, the greatest gift was simply being together.

David and Itai participated in the life of the community, interacted with our members, and spent time with our children.

The atmosphere was one of friendship and family.

The Shabbat reminded us that Jewish life can bring people together across countries, cultures, and continents.

We are grateful to David and Itai for sharing this special Shabbat with us.

May the friendship between Nasenyi and our friends in Israel continue to grow.

Shabbat Shalom!

title: David and Itai’s Visit to Nasenyi Jewish Community
body:
On Friday, 7 August 2026, the Nasenyi Jewish Community in eastern Uganda had the pleasure of welcoming two special guests from Israel, David Yair and Itai Mayar.

Their visit was more than a simple trip to Uganda. It was an opportunity to strengthen the connection between the Nasenyi community and fellow Jews from Israel and to share Jewish learning, culture, friendship, and Shabbat together.

The connection began earlier in the year when Noam visited Nasenyi. Through that relationship, David and Itai were later connected with the community through Jonathan Mwosuko, who received them and helped bring them to Nasenyi.

Although their visit lasted only from Friday, 7 August to Sunday, 9 August, it created many meaningful memories for the community.

Sharing Jewish Life Together

From the moment they arrived, David and Itai became part of the community.

They spent time with the children, teaching them Hebrew, Israeli songs, and games. The children were excited to interact with visitors from Israel and had the opportunity to learn in a relaxed and enjoyable environment.

For a community such as Nasenyi, opportunities like these are particularly valuable. Jewish education and access to Hebrew learning materials and teachers remain important areas of growth for the community.

Nasenyi is part of Uganda’s historic Abayudaya Jewish community, which has maintained Jewish religious and cultural life in eastern Uganda for generations. Today, Abayudaya communities continue to strengthen their Jewish identity through worship, education, Torah study, and connections with Jewish communities around the world.

A Meaningful Shabbat

The highlight of the visit was Shabbat on Saturday, 8 August.

David participated in the Torah service and was invited to read from the Torah. He read beautifully and fluently in Hebrew, creating a special moment for the congregation.

David and Itai also shared Divrei Torah with the community. Their teachings gave everyone an opportunity to learn, reflect, and exchange perspectives.

The visit demonstrated something very important: Jewish communities may live thousands of kilometres apart, but Torah, Shabbat, Hebrew, learning, and friendship can bring people together.

A Friendship We Hope Will Continue

What impressed the community most was the humility and friendliness of David and Itai.

They interacted naturally with everyone and especially enjoyed spending time with the children. Their visit did not feel like strangers coming to visit strangers. Instead, it felt like members of one Jewish family coming together.

Their three-day visit may have ended, but the friendship and memories created during those days will remain with the Nasenyi community.

We thank David and Itai for visiting Nasenyi, sharing Torah, teaching our children, and bringing their warmth and friendship to our community.

Our doors will always be open to you.

Todah Rabbah, David and Itai. Until we meet again — להתראות! 🇮🇱❤️

title: How the Nasenyi Jewish Community Serves Through Education, Health, and Agriculture
body:
How the Nasenyi Jewish Community Serves Through Education, Health, and Agriculture

Learn how the Nasenyi Jewish Community supports families through education, healthcare initiatives, agriculture, and community development rooted in Jewish values and service.

Introduction

For the Nasenyi Jewish Community, faith is expressed not only through prayer and synagogue worship, but also through practical service to people. Education, health, and agriculture are central pillars of community life, reflecting the Jewish values of compassion, responsibility, and care for one another.

Education: Building the Next Generation

Education is one of the community’s highest priorities. Children are encouraged to grow both academically and spiritually, learning Hebrew, Torah, Jewish traditions, and the skills needed for daily life.

Access to books, learning materials, desks, and educational resources remains an important need, and community leaders continue working to create better opportunities for young people. Every investment in education strengthens the future of the entire community.

Health and Community Well-Being

Good health is essential for families to thrive. The Nasenyi community promotes healthcare awareness, preventive care, and support for vulnerable members of society. Community initiatives seek to improve access to medical services and ensure that children, mothers, and elders receive the care they need.

Health programs are viewed as an extension of the Jewish principle of preserving life and human dignity.

Agriculture as a Source of Sustainability

Most families in Nasenyi depend on agriculture for their livelihoods. Farming provides food, income, and stability, making agricultural development an important part of community resilience.

Improving farming methods, increasing food security, and supporting smallholder farmers are practical ways the community works toward long-term sustainability. Agriculture is not only an economic activity—it is a way of caring for creation and providing for future generations.

Serving Together

One of the defining strengths of Nasenyi is the spirit of cooperation. Families help one another during harvests, celebrations, times of illness, and moments of need. This culture of mutual support reflects the deep communal values that have sustained the Abayudaya people for more than a century.

Conclusion

The Nasenyi Jewish Community demonstrates that a synagogue can be more than a place of worship. Through education, healthcare, agriculture, and acts of kindness, the community continues to serve its members while preserving a vibrant Jewish presence in rural Uganda.

As Nasenyi looks to the future, these efforts remain essential to ensuring that faith, culture, and community continue to flourish together for generations to come.

title: Preserving Abayudaya Culture and Jewish Identity in Rural Uganda
body:
Preserving Abayudaya Culture and Jewish Identity in Uganda

Explore how the Nasenyi Jewish Community preserves Hebrew prayer, Torah learning, Jewish festivals, music, and cultural traditions while strengthening future generations in rural Uganda.

Introduction

The Abayudaya Jewish community of Uganda represents one of the most distinctive expressions of Jewish life in the world. In Nasenyi, Jewish identity has been preserved not only through religious observance, but also through language, music, education, and community life. For more than a century, the people of Nasenyi have demonstrated that Jewish tradition can thrive while remaining deeply rooted in local Ugandan culture.

The Meaning of Abayudaya

The word Abayudaya comes from Luganda and means “People of Judah.” It reflects a community that embraced Judaism through conviction and commitment rather than through ancient ancestry. Over the years, the Abayudaya have developed a rich religious culture that combines traditional Jewish practice with the rhythms, harmonies, and languages of eastern Uganda.

Worship in Hebrew and Luganda

One of the most beautiful aspects of Nasenyi’s religious life is the way Hebrew prayer exists alongside Luganda and other local languages. Congregational singing often features African musical styles while maintaining the structure and meaning of Jewish liturgy.

This musical heritage has become an important part of Abayudaya identity. It allows younger generations to connect with Judaism through familiar cultural forms while remaining faithful to Jewish tradition.

Festivals That Bring the Community Together

Throughout the year, the synagogue becomes a gathering place for celebrations of Passover, Shavuot, Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, Sukkot, and other Jewish festivals. These occasions strengthen family bonds, reinforce Torah teachings, and remind community members of their shared history.

Children, youth, and elders participate together, ensuring that traditions are learned through experience as well as instruction.

Education as Cultural Preservation

For the Nasenyi Jewish Community, education is inseparable from cultural survival. Hebrew literacy, Torah study, Jewish history, and religious practice are all viewed as essential foundations for the future of the community.

Parents and teachers work together to ensure that children understand not only the rituals of Judaism, but also the story of how their community came to embrace and preserve the faith in Uganda.

Looking Toward the Future

Preserving culture requires more than remembering the past—it requires investing in the future. The Nasenyi community continues to encourage youth leadership, education, and spiritual development so that the next generation can carry forward the values of faith, compassion, and communal responsibility.

Conclusion

The preservation of Abayudaya culture in Nasenyi is a remarkable example of how identity can be maintained through worship, education, music, and shared memory. In a rapidly changing world, the community’s commitment to its Jewish heritage remains a powerful source of hope and continuity.
